highlights: A persistent QuickAgent gets the time, tasks, a memory, skills and stored secrets only when its release declares them.
An installed agent can keep tasks that fire on time, a memory it compacts and recalls, and its own name and persona.
You can let an installed agent write in your Writing Voice; it is off until you switch it on.
When agentry runhost add or remove refuses a server's address or host key, the message names the runhost.
agentry agent install adds a persistent QuickAgent from the registry, or your own folder with --local.
An installed agent keeps its conversation and files between starts, and runs with the knowledge it ships.
It takes on the persona its publisher gave it, which you can rename and, unless locked, replace.
Two publishers' agents of the same name run side by side; agentry agent uninstall keeps their data unless asked.
agentry runhost add sets up a Linux server you own as a remote runhost, over SSH.
Setup checks the server first, then installs Docker, gVisor and this CLI, and opens no network port.
Your computer gets its own key for the runhost, which runs nothing but the runhost's service.
agentry runhost list, status, doctor and remove look after each runhost.
login, setup, install and validate end with the next step to take.
When the container engine or the registry cannot be reached, the CLI names which and how to fix it.
agentry doctor ends every failed check with a fix line and checks your sign-in, CLI version and PATH.
setup warns when the key variable is unset and defaults to each provider's newest model; --quiet and --verbose.
A run ends with a summary: its files, how long it took, what it cost where known, and where its receipts are.
A failed run names its exit class in words, the cause, the receipts folder, and whether a retry is likely to help.
agentry runs lists the runs made from here and agentry open opens one's folder; run --dry-run says the plan in words.
Every exit class has one name and meaning, shared by run --help, the summary and the result's JSON.
agentry info shows how to run a QuickAgent: its questions and how to answer each, its files, its keys and its guide.
agentry info --json carries the same, so an agent driving the CLI can answer the questions with --intake.
The Assistant and Agentry Helper work out how to run a QuickAgent from its own questions, files and guide.
Asked to run a QuickAgent on a repository, they give it the repository's address instead of asking you to download it.
Runs use the newest Docker Agent, MCP gateway and Codex, and every runtime image is rebuilt with current fixes.
Declared npm servers run on Node 26 and PyPI servers on Python 3.15, or on Python 3.14 when a server needs it.
A run stops before it starts when a tool filter names a tool in the wrong case, and says the exact name to use.
The Drafter's knowledge of the runtime is updated to match.
When a draft's instructions use a tool the agent was not given, the Drafter now fixes the draft before handing it back.
